title: DraftAttention: Fast Video Diffusion via Low-Resolution Attention Guidance
original_abstract: Diffusion transformer–based video generation models (DiTs) have recently attracted widespread attention for their excellent generation quality. However, their computational cost remains a major bottleneck—attention alone accounts for over 80% of total latency, and generating just 8 seconds of 720p video takes tens of minutes—posing serious challenges to practical application and scalability. To address this, we propose the DraftAttention, a training-free framework for the acceleration of video diffusion transformers with dynamic sparse attention on GPUs. We apply down-sampling to each feature map across frames in the compressed latent space, enabling a higher-level receptive field over the latent composed of hundreds of thousands of tokens. The low-resolution draft attention map, derived from draft query and key, exposes redundancy both spatially within each feature map and temporally across frames. We reorder the query, key, and value based on the draft attention map to guide the sparse attention computation in full resolution, and subsequently restore their original order after the attention computation. This reordering enables structured sparsity that aligns with hardware-optimized execution. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that the low-resolution draft attention closely approximates the full attention, providing reliable guidance for constructing accurate sparse attention. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing sparse attention approaches in video generation quality and achieves up to 1.75× end-to-end speedup on GPUs.

innovations.name: Low-Resolution Draft Attention
innovations.description: Uses 8×16 average pooling to create low-resolution draft attention map that identifies important regions across spatial and temporal dimensions

innovations.name: Hardware-Friendly Reordering
innovations.description: Deterministic token reordering to align sparse patterns with GPU memory layout for efficient block processing
innovations.runtime_improvement: O(n) reordering overhead, enables coalesced memory access

innovations.name: Theoretical Error Bounds
innovations.description: Provides formal bounds on approximation error between full and draft attention using Frobenius norm analysis

innovations.name: Training-Free Integration
innovations.description: Plug-and-play module requiring no additional training or fine-tuning

improvements.name: Adaptive Kernel Selection
improvements.description: Content-aware pooling kernel selection based on local complexity analysis
improvements.runtime_improvement: [n, d, k] → [n/g'(x), d, k'(x)] where g' varies by content

improvements.name: Dynamic Sparsity Scheduling
improvements.description: Step-wise sparsity adjustment based on attention entropy across denoising steps

improvements.name: Hierarchical Draft Attention
improvements.description: Multi-scale draft attention with learned combination weights
improvements.runtime_improvement: Σ_i [g_i, g_i, d] + [r·n, n, d] for multiple scales

improvements.name: Temporal-Separate Pooling
improvements.description: Different pooling strategies for spatial vs temporal dimensions
improvements.runtime_improvement: [t, h, w] → [t', h', w'] with t' ≠ h' ≠ w'

improvements.name: Quantization Integration
improvements.description: Combine with INT8/INT4 weight quantization for additional memory reduction
improvements.runtime_improvement: [g, g, d/4] + [r·n, n, d/4] for INT4 quantization

improvements.name: Distributed Inference Support
improvements.description: Split draft attention across GPUs with efficient communication

experimental_parameters.fallback_steps: First 25% of denoising steps use full attention

runtime_comparison.baseline_dense: [n, n, d] - Full quadratic complexity O(n²d)
runtime_comparison.draft_attention: [n/128, n/128, d] + [r·n, n, d] - Reduced to O(n²d/128² + r·n²d)
runtime_comparison.improved_adaptive: [n/g'(x), n/g'(x), d] + [r(t)·n, n, d] - Dynamic complexity based on content
